In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
chemotherapy of primary malignant brain tumor in children has been disappointing, but there are encouraging reports that the outlook may be better than was previously thought.
chemotherapy of brain tumors in children remains largely experimental and that no agent or combination is clearly superior.

there is no proven effective chemotherapy for the malignant brain tumors in childhood, although a few agents have been used successfully in some children with medulloblastomata and ependymomata, and some agents have been used with apparent success in children with brain‐stem gliomata.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of chemotherapy for children with brain tumors is still in the investigational stage, and that the best results are obtained in children with medulloblastomatous tumors.
the use of chemotherapy in children with malignant brain tumors has been disappointing, with few exceptions.
